stubs.angle: Why does a typical Dockerfile for a .NET app use a multi-stage build with the SDK image for building and the ASP.NET runtime image for the final stage?
stubs.answerHinge: Only the last stage becomes the shipped image, so the SDK, sources and intermediate build output stay out of it, which makes the image smaller and reduces its attack surface.

stubs.angle: Which statement correctly distinguishes continuous delivery from continuous deployment?
stubs.answerHinge: In continuous delivery every change is kept releasable and production release is a manual business decision, while in continuous deployment every change that passes the pipeline goes to production automatically.

stubs.angle: Which HTTP header carries the trace id and parent span id between services under the W3C Trace Context standard used by default in .NET?
stubs.answerHinge: The traceparent header carries the version, trace id, parent span id and trace flags; tracestate only carries vendor-specific data.

stubs.angle: What are logs, metrics and traces, and what question about a running service is each one best at answering?
stubs.answerHinge: Metrics are cheap aggregated numbers that show that something is wrong, traces show where in a request path across services time or errors occur, and logs give the detailed event context of why.

stubs.angle: Find the line in a .NET Dockerfile that makes every source change re-run dotnet restore and download all packages again.
stubs.answerHinge: COPY . . placed before dotnet restore invalidates the restore layer on any file change; copying only the project files first and restoring before copying the rest keeps the restore layer cached.

stubs.angle: After moving an app to the .NET 8 ASP.NET Core container images, the orchestrator still sends traffic to port 80 and gets no answer; which port does the app listen on by default?
stubs.answerHinge: Starting with .NET 8 the official ASP.NET Core images set ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS to 8080 instead of listening on port 80.

stubs.angle: Which ways of writing a log call with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging keep OrderId as a separate structured property in the log sink?
stubs.answerHinge: A message template with named placeholders and a [LoggerMessage] source-generated method keep structured properties, while string interpolation and concatenation bake the values into a flat message string.

stubs.angle: Which System.Diagnostics.Metrics instrument should record the duration of each processed request so that dashboards can show p95 and p99?
stubs.answerHinge: A Histogram records a distribution of values from which percentiles can be computed, whereas a Counter only sums and an UpDownCounter tracks a current total.

stubs.angle: Find the line in BCL code using ActivitySource that throws NullReferenceException when no tracing listener is registered.
stubs.answerHinge: ActivitySource.StartActivity returns null when no ActivityListener samples the source, so calling SetTag on the result without a null-conditional operator throws.

stubs.angle: Which tags are safe to attach to an HTTP request duration metric without blowing up the number of time series in the metrics backend?
stubs.answerHinge: Bounded values such as route template, HTTP method and status code are safe, while user id, raw URL path with ids or request id create unbounded cardinality and exhaust backend memory.

stubs.angle: When would you choose a blue-green deployment over a canary release for a high-traffic service, and what does each cost you?
stubs.answerHinge: Blue-green gives an instant full switch and rollback at the price of double capacity and exposing all users at once, while canary limits blast radius by gradual traffic shifting but needs per-version metrics, longer rollouts and both versions coexisting.

stubs.angle: Tracing is configured with 1% head-based sampling and the traces of the rare failing requests you need to investigate are almost never recorded; what do you change?
stubs.answerHinge: Head sampling decides before the outcome is known, so keeping error and slow traces requires tail-based sampling in a collector (or a parent-based policy plus always-sampled errors) while accepting its buffering cost.

stubs.angle: Your pipeline rebuilds the app separately for staging and production, and a production bug cannot be reproduced on staging; what process change do you drive with the team and how do you roll it out?
stubs.answerHinge: Build one immutable versioned artifact or image once and promote that exact artifact through environments, with environment differences supplied only by configuration, so what was tested is what ships.

stubs.angle: How do you roll out a breaking database schema change used by several independently deployed services that update with rolling deployments and no downtime?
stubs.answerHinge: Use expand-contract (parallel change): add the new schema alongside the old, make every service version compatible with both, migrate data, and remove the old schema only after no running version depends on it.
